hypothesis: The neuron responds selectively to prominent circular or arcuate structures, most consistently activating for automobile wheels and circular mechanical components such as projector lenses, weight plates, and oil filters. The neuron is invariant to object category—ranging from cars and electronics to organic curves like a snake or bird neck—as well as lighting and texture, provided the sharp curvature and tonal polarity are preserved. The activating features, typically silver, white, black, or dark grey, appear against neutral, desaturated backgrounds of light gray, beige, or out-of-focus natural tones. The feature typically occupies 25–50% of the image surface and is frequently positioned in the lower-left quadrant or centered within the frame.
